title: Asian Markets Start the Week Mixed as Investors Rethink the AI Trade Amid Global Crosscurrents
excerpt: South Korean chip stocks slide on AI spending doubts while Chinese equities outperform on policy optimism.
body:
• Asian equities opened the week with a mixed performance on Monday as investors weighed growing doubts about the pace of AI monetisation against resilient economic data.
  • South Korean markets led declines, with semiconductor stocks under pressure after recent signals that major hyperscalers may be reassessing the pace of AI capital expenditure.
  • Chinese equities outperformed the region on policy optimism, with Beijing's latest stimulus signals lifting sentiment despite lingering property sector concerns.
  • The session sets the stage for a pivotal week of global tech earnings, with Alphabet and Tesla reporting Tuesday and Intel later in the week.

AI Spending Doubts Weigh on Chip Stocks

Asian markets started the trading week on an uneven footing Monday, with the technology sector bearing the brunt of a reassessment that has been building since last week's selloff in global chip stocks. South Korea's KOSPI fell as semiconductor heavyweights — key suppliers to the global AI infrastructure buildout — faced renewed selling pressure.

The catalyst is growing scepticism among institutional investors about whether the massive capital expenditure commitments made by hyperscalers like Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta will translate into proportional revenue returns quickly enough. With Big Tech's combined AI-related capex projected to exceed $725 billion, questions about the timeline from spending to monetisation have intensified.

The concerns echo earlier cycles of infrastructure overinvestment, though bulls point to BofA's estimate that enterprise AI spending will more than double to $1.7 trillion, suggesting the demand runway remains long even if near-term returns disappoint.

China Bucks the Trend

Chinese equities stood apart from the regional weakness, with mainland and Hong Kong-listed shares posting gains on Monday. Beijing's latest round of policy signals — including hints at additional fiscal support for the property sector and measures to boost domestic consumption — lifted sentiment among investors who have been underweight China for much of 2026.

The divergence underscores a broader rotation playing out across Asian markets: money flowing out of the richly-valued AI supply chain and into markets where valuations are lower and policy tailwinds are building.

What to Watch This Week

The session sets up what may be the most consequential global earnings week of the quarter. Alphabet and Tesla report on Tuesday, with investors watching Google's cloud and AI revenue growth as a bellwether for enterprise AI adoption. Intel reports later in the week, offering a read on semiconductor demand beyond the top-tier AI chips that have dominated the narrative.

For Indian markets, the week brings its own blockbuster calendar. Infosys, IndiGo, Paytm, and Bajaj Auto are among the marquee names reporting quarterly results, while foreign institutional investors — who returned to Indian equities last week after a four-month, $29 billion selloff — will be watching for signals on IT services demand and domestic consumption trends.

The Indian rupee remains under pressure from elevated oil prices driven by the ongoing Iran-US conflict, adding another variable for NRI investors managing cross-border portfolios. Brent crude's move above $90 per barrel has amplified concerns about India's import bill and current account deficit, even as the RBI has flagged Middle East instability as a key risk to the nation's growth outlook.
